What is the CDI (and why CDBs are "% of the CDI")

The CDI is the average rate of one-day loans that banks make to each other. It closely tracks the Selic rate and is the benchmark of Brazilian fixed income. When a CDB promises "110% of the CDI", it pays 1.10 times the period CDI. That is why the calculator asks for a percentage: the gain in reais depends on the CDI rate reported by the Central Bank.

CDBs pay income tax on the gain; LCI and LCA are tax-exempt for individuals. Comparing only the CDI percentage is misleading. Pocket rule "the 112.5% rule": between 6 and 12 months, an LCI at 90% of the CDI matches a CDB at 112.5% of the CDI (90 ÷ 0.80). At the same percentage, the LCI wins — and the shorter the term, the bigger the effect. The Compare tab shows the exact winner.
Tesouro Selic and the market price

Tesouro Selic pays close to the Selic rate, updated every business day. Held to maturity, the gain follows the agreed rate. But the bond is marked to market: sold early, the price may carry a discount or a premium, and the real return changes. The app applies only the contracted rate — it does not calculate the discount or early-sale costs.

IPCA+ pays the inflation measured by the IPCA plus a real rate set at purchase. "Protection" means that purchasing power follows inflation: if the IPCA rises, the return rises with it. The app combines both parts: annual = (1 + IPCA) × (1 + real rate) − 1. Example: 6% IPCA with a 6.20% real rate yields ≈ 12.57% a year.

Fixed-income tax is regressive: the longer the money stays invested, the lower the rate. Up to 6 months: 22.5%. From 6 to 12 months: 20%. From 1 to 2 years: 17.5%. Above 2 years: 15%. Note: tax applies only to the gain (the yield), never to the amount invested. The app deducts the term tax in every simulation.

With compound interest, each month yields on the whole balance: interest starts generating interest. App example: R$ 1,000.00 at 0.7% a month for 12 months becomes R$ 1,087.31. The math is 1,000 × 1.007¹². Early months earn little; the curve accelerates toward the end — that is what the evolution chart shows.

The rates come from the Central Bank open series: the CDI, the Selic rate and the IPCA are fetched from the internet. The "BCB · dd/mm" badge shows the update date. The values stay cached for 24 hours. Without internet, the app uses the last valid value or the local fallback — the screen never freezes.

The app calculates in uniform months (12 months ≈ 1 year), not in exact calendar days — the real maturity may shift by days. There is no come-cotas (the semi-annual tax prepayment of funds) and no IOF for redemptions within 30 days. It also does not simulate a discounted early Tesouro sale or the LCI/LCA grace period. Treat the numbers as an estimate.
